Hypercalcemia

parathyroid hormone first in every case · calcium and phosphorus patterns · normal labs that rule out alternativesIs the parathyroid hormone high or suppressed, and which way is the phosphorus going?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Confirmed high calcium: PTH (parathyroid hormone) first. High or inappropriately normal primary hyperparathyroidism or familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (FHH); suppressed malignancy, vitamin D or granulomas
  • High PTH with high urine calcium primary hyperparathyroidism, surgery; calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio under 1% FHH, no surgery
  • Severe or confused: isotonic saline first calcitonin and a bisphosphonate
What it is

Total calcium over 10.4 mg/dL; stones, bones, groans, thrones and psychiatric overtones

Driver

PTH (primary hyperparathyroidism, the commonest, usually an adenoma), PTHrP (parathyroid hormone-related protein) from a tumor, calcitriol from granulomas or lymphoma, bone resorption from metastases, myeloma or immobilization

Triggers

Thiazides; lithium; calcium carbonate antacids (milk-alkali); vitamin D excess; immobilization

Chain

PTH or PTHrP bone resorption and renal phosphate loss high calcium, low phosphate

High calcium urine cannot concentrate polyuria and volume depletion calcium rises further

Insights

Phosphate splits the drivers: low with PTH or PTHrP, high with vitamin D or immobilization

A calcium over 13 points away from the parathyroid

2Urgent risks
SevereCalcium 14 or more, confusion, dehydration
Short QT interval on the ECG (electrocardiogram); arrhythmias

If calcium is severe or the patient is confused, choose isotonic saline first, then calcitonin and a bisphosphonate.

5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: hypercalcemia Calcium – total over 10.4 mg/dL · PTH-driven – PTH high or inappropriately normal · FHH – calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio under 1%

7Treatment
1

Severesevere or symptomatic

Isotonic saline first: nearly all are volume depleted
In practiceIn practice: a clinical reference gives isotonic saline plus a loop diuretic; the board answer keeps the loop diuretic for fluid overload, because it deepens volume depletion.
2

Addcalcium still high

Calcitonin for fast, short control and a bisphosphonate for lasting control

Bisphosphonates are usually the drugs of choice in malignancy.

3

Calcitriolgranulomas, lymphoma, vitamin D toxicity

Add a glucocorticoid
4

Dialysissevere symptoms, or renal failure

Hemodialysis with a low-calcium bath

Practice
  1. 58 yo F with calcium 11.6 and phosphorus 2.1, found incidentally → Check PTH first
  2. 58 yo F with calcium 11.6 and an elevated PTH → Primary hyperparathyroidism
  3. 58 yo F with calcium 13.4, suppressed PTH and weight loss → Malignancy → PTHrP and imaging
  4. 24 yo M with lifelong mild hypercalcemia, normal PTH and a urine calcium-creatinine clearance ratio under 0.01 → Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia → no surgery
  5. 58 yo F with hypercalcemia, suppressed PTH, high 1,25-OH vitamin D and hilar adenopathy → Granulomatous disease
  6. 58 yo F with calcium 14.5, confusion and dehydration → Isotonic saline first, then calcitonin and a bisphosphonate
Normal labs that rule out alternatives A normal albumin means the calcium is truly elevated, with no correction needed · a specific gravity of 1.005 argues against diabetes mellitus, because glucosuria raises the specific gravity · low phosphorus argues against vitamin D excess, which raises both calcium and phosphorus · enalapril rather than a thiazide removes the drug confounder.
Pairs with Part I Polyuria covers the polyuria hypercalcemia causes. It results from an acquired, reversible resistance to vasopressin at the collecting duct, which corrects when the calcium does. Ask: does the kidney concentrate after desmopressin?
